summary_en: Paul VI's motu proprio Mysterii paschalis approves the Normae universales de anno liturgico et de Calendario and the new Calendarium Romanum generale for the whole Latin Church, in force from 1 January 1970; the Normae follow at pp. 165-176 (pdf 51-62) and the Calendarium at pp. 177-186 (pdf 63-72), with the interim Schema Calendarii generalis pro anno 1970 at pp. 187-202 (pdf 73-88).
excerpt: Huiusmodi ergo causis diligentissime coram Domino perpensis, novum Calendarium Romanum generale a Consilio ad exsequendam Constitutionem de Sacra Liturgia compositum, itemque normas universales ad ordinationem anni liturgici spectantes, Apostolica Nostra auctoritate approbamus, ut a die I mensis Ianuarii proximi anni MCMLXX vigere incipiant

summary_en: Decree of the Sacred Congregation of Rites promulgating the Normae universales and the Calendarium Romanum generale approved by Mysterii paschalis, in force 1 January 1970, with interim rules for using the new Calendar with the old books (solemnities/feasts/memorials treated as I/II/III class feasts, Baptism of the Lord and Christ the King on their new days, suppressed feasts no longer celebrated in the Roman rite but retainable in particular calendars, transferred saints kept on their old day until the new books, newly inscribed saints as optional memorials) and ordering that all diocesan and religious calendars and Propers be conformed to the new general Calendar.
excerpt: Anni liturgici ordinatione atque generali Calendario Romano a Summo Pontifice PAULO PP. VI approbatis, per Litteras Apostolicas Mysterii paschalis celebrationem die 14 februarii 1969 motu proprio datas, Sacra haec Congregatio, de speciali mandato eiusdem Summi Pontificis ea promulgat, statuens ut a die 1 ianuarii proximi anni 1970 vigere incipiant.

summary_en: Instruction of the Congregation for Divine Worship on accommodating particular calendars 'ad interim' for 1970 until the typical editions are complete: celebrations also in the general Calendar follow it; proper celebrations hitherto in particular calendars are kept, I-class feasts as solemnities, II-class as feasts, III-class as obligatory memorials (one chosen when they coincide with a general obligatory memorial), commemorations as optional memorials or omitted; the same applies to feasts of Beati. Kind is 'other' because it is a general norm about every particular calendar rather than a change to one of them.
excerpt: Interim, pro anno 1970 et donec editio typica librorum liturgicorum completa sit, haec serventur: 1. Celebrationes, quae etiam in Calendario generali inscribuntur, eadem ratione, qua in eo recensentur, peragantur. 2. Celebrationes propriae usque adhuc in Calendariis particularibus inscriptae, retineantur, et recolantur eadem ratione ac celebrationes in Calendario generali retentae

summary_en: Corrigenda to the printed volume Calendarium Romanum (1969): 'Ss.mae Eucharistiae' in Normae n. 7 is to read 'SS.mi Corporis Christi'; the apposition 'presbyteri' is to be deleted after the names of S. Paulus Miki and S. Hieronymus Emiliani; further corrections to the historical commentary (list of saints removed from the Calendar, place of death of S. Romuald, year of death of S. Maria Goretti, place of death of S. John Capistran, memorial of Ss. Bacchus and Apuleius, geographical index). No protocol or date is printed; the same Hieronymus Emiliani correction appears as a footnote on p. 178 of the Calendar in Notitiae 46.
excerpt: In volumine Calendarium Romanum (Typis Polyglottis Vaticanis 1969), quaedam menda irrepserunt, quae corrigenda sunt uti sequitur: p. 12, n. 7: loco Ss.mae Eucharistiae: SS.mi Corporis Christi p. 24, 41, 164: post nomen S. Pauli Miki, tollatur appositio presbyteri. p. 24, 45, 170: item post nomen S. Hieronymi Emiliani, tollatur appositio presbyteri.

summary_en: Documentorum explanatio, 'Ad Calendarium' (nn. 5-8), unofficial responses of the Congregation: Holy Family and Baptism of the Lord have I Vespers (the printed 'Negative' in the answer to n. 5 is struck through by hand on the page); the Mass of the II Sunday after Christmas is that of the new Missal; with the Vigil of Ascension abolished the Mass is of the preceding Sunday and the Office for 1970 as in the Breviary; and, for regions transferring Epiphany, Ascension and Corpus Christi to Sunday, a day-by-day calendar for 4-12 January, 6-10 May and 28-31 May 1970. The page states these solutions have orientative, not official, value.
excerpt: 8. Quomodo ordinanda est celebratio Missae et Officii divini in regionibus ubi sollemnitates Epiphaniae et Ascensionis Domini ac Corporis Christi in dominicam transferuntur? Resp.: Attenta declaratione anno praeterito facta a Sacra Congregatione Rituum (Cf. Notitiae, vol. IV, 1968, p. 279), adveniente anno 1970, ubi supradictae sollemnitates in dominicam transferuntur, celebrentur secundum Calendarium quod sequitur

summary_en: For the Proper of all Australia: St Patrick is raised to the grade of solemnity, St Peter Chanel to obligatory memorial, and the feasts of St Bridget, St Columba and Bl. Oliver Plunket are removed.
excerpt: Australia, 2 sept. 1969 (Prot. n. 1109/69): conceditur ut S. Patricius celebretur gradu sollemnitatis, S. Petrus Chanel gradu memoriae obligatoriae et festa Ss. Birgittae, Columbae et B. Oliverii Plunket exspungantur e Proprio totius Australiae.

summary_en: For England and Wales: St David (1 March) is celebrated as a solemnity in Wales and a feast in England; St George (23 April) as a solemnity in England and a feast in Wales.
excerpt: Anglia-Cambria, 24 sept. 1969 (Prot. n. 1102/69): conceditur ut die 1 martii S. David celebretur gradu sollemnitatis in Cambria, gradu festi in Anglia; die 23 aprilis S. Georgius celebretur gradu sollemnitatis in Anglia, gradu festi in Cambria.

summary_en: The proper Calendar and Offices of the diocese of Lodi (Laudensis), revised according to the Instruction of the Congregation of Rites of 14 February 1961, are approved. Two protocol numbers are printed; the id uses the first.
excerpt: Italia, Laudensis: 14 iulii 1969 (Prot. n. 542/69 et 721/69): probantur Calendarium et Officia Propria, recognita iuxta Instructionem S. C. Rituum, diei 14 febr. 1961.

summary_en: Venezuela is allowed the colour blue on the solemnity of the Immaculate Conception and in her votive Masses, and black on Good Friday, in place of the red prescribed by the Institutio generalis. Recorded as 'other' because it concerns liturgical colour, not the content or rank of a calendar; may be out of scope.
excerpt: Venetiola, 8 aug. 1969 (Prot. n. 938/69): conceditur ut in sollemnitate Immaculatae Conceptionis B. V. M. et in eiusdem Missis votivis color caeruleus adhibeatur, et feria VI Hebdomadae Sanctae color niger.

summary_en: The Order of Preachers may adopt the Missale Romanum and the Normae universales with the new Calendarium Romanum generale and the Litany of Saints for the whole Order; ad interim, until its own particular calendar is approved, the Order's I-class saints (B.M.V. a Rosario, S. Dominicus, S. Thomas Aquinas, S. Catharina Senensis) become solemnities, II-class feasts remain feasts, III-class saints and Beati become obligatory memorials, and the rest optional memorials.
excerpt: Dum Calendarium particulare definitivum Ordinis rite paratum sit et approbatum, ad interim, Sancti Ordinis Fratrum Praedicatorum qui celebrantur tamquam festa I classis, habeantur tamquam Sollemnitates (nempe, B. M. V. a Rosario, S. Dominici, S. Thomae Aquinatis et S. Catharinae Senensis); qui vero recensentur tamquam festa II classis, tamquam « festa » recolantur

summary_en: The Cistercian Order may use the new Roman Breviary throughout the Order, and the monks and monasteries that do so are to follow the Calendarium Romanum with the Order's Proper added.
excerpt: Sacer Ordo Cisterciensis: 3 sept. 1969 (Prot. n. 973/69): conceditur ut in universo Ordine novum Breviarium romanum adhiberi valeat, ita tamen ut in recitatione chorali adhibeatur si Superior cum voto capituli conventualis ita statuerit, et monachi et monasteria qui Officium divinum secundum Breviarium romanum celebrabunt, sequantur etiam Calendarium Romanum, addito « Proprio » Ordinis.

summary_en: The proper Calendar of the Order of St Benedict, adapted to the new Roman Calendar, is approved for two years.
excerpt: Ordo Sancti Benedicti, 7 iulii 1969 (Prot. n. 623/69): probatur « ad biennium » Calendarium proprium O.S.B., aptatum novo Calendario Romano.

target.institute: Ordo Fratrum Discalceatorum B. M. V. a Monte Carmelo

summary_en: The Discalced Carmelites may, for five years, keep a Commemoration of all the deceased of the Order on 15 November in their proper calendar.
excerpt: Ordo Fratrum Discalceatorum B. M. V. a Monte Carmelo, 7 aug. 1969 (Prot. n. 933/69): conceditur « ad quinquennium » ut in Calendario proprio die 15 novembris fiat Commemoratio omnium defunctorum Ordinis.

summary_en: The Redemptorists may celebrate St Clement Mary Hofbauer on 16 March 1970 with the grade of feast, for that year only, the 150th anniversary of his death.
excerpt: Congregatio SS.mi Redemptoris, 18 iulii 1969 (Prot. n. 826/69): conceditur ut festum S. Clementis Mariae Hofbauer, Presbyteri, die 16 martii celebrari possit, pro anno 1970, tamquam festum. Nam illo die complentur 150 anni ab eius morte.

summary_en: The Rogationists may, for ten years, celebrate votive Masses of the Most Holy Name of Jesus in their churches and oratories on 31 January, unless a solemnity occurs. Recorded as 'other' with review because it is a votive-Mass indult tied to a fixed annual date rather than a calendar inscription.
excerpt: Congregatio Rogationistarum a Corde Iesu, 19 iulii 1969 (Prot. n. 510/69): conceditur « ad decennium » ut in ecclesiis et oratoriis Congregationis celebrentur Missae votivae de SS.mo Nomine Iesu, die 31 ianuarii, dummodo non occurrat sollemnitas.

summary_en: For 1970 only, in the diocese of Valencia the feast of St Vincent Ferrer is kept on 6 April (its traditional date in the Valencian region) and the solemnity of the Annunciation, displaced by Holy Week that year, on the following day, 7 April.
excerpt: Hispania: Valentina, 23 iulii 1969 (Prot. n. 846/69): conceditur ut pro anno 1970 festum S. Vincentii Ferrer celebretur die 6 aprilis et Sollemnitas Annuntiationis Domini, die sequenti, cum inde ab antiquis temporibus die 6 aprilis in regione Valentina celebretur sollemnitas S. Vincentii Ferrer.

summary_en: The diocese of Greensburg (USA), where Bl. John Nepomucene Neumann exercised pastoral ministry, may celebrate his feast on 7 January as an obligatory memorial.
excerpt: U.S.A.: Greensburgensis, 23 iulii 1969 (Prot. n. 833/69): conceditur ut festum B. Ioannis Nepomuceni Neumann, qui in dioecesi et in civitate Greensburgensi ministerium pastorale exercuit, celebrari possit die 7 ianuarii, tamquam Memoria obligatoria.

summary_en: In the diocese of Treviso the titular saints of the parish church of Ss. Leonard and Roch at Ponzano Veneto may be celebrated together on 6 November. Listed under 'X. Varia'; it concerns a single parish, not the diocesan calendar, hence 'other' with review. The same protocol number is also printed under 'VIII. Missae votivae in Sanctuariis' for a Treviso sanctuary (p. 363), which is not recorded.
excerpt: Tarvisina, 3 sept. 1969 (Prot. n. 981/69): conceditur ut sancti titulares ecclesiae paroecialis SS. Leonardi et Rochi in pago v. « Ponzano Veneto » communi celebratione recolantur die 6 novembris.

summary_en: Documentorum explanatio, 'Ad Calendarium' (nn. 16-21), unofficial responses: the anniversary of dedication and the solemnity of the principal patron of the place or of the title of one's own church may be transferred to a Sunday per annum or of Christmastide but not to Sundays of Advent, Lent or Easter or Sundays with a general solemnity (and not for the cathedral, a regional or national patron or a secondary patron); church titles are not to be changed even when the saint is no longer in the general Calendar; no commemoration of the weekday on solemnities in Advent and Lent; Rogations and Ember Days follow the episcopal conference or bishop; no vigil Mass of Christmas on the morning of 24 December.
excerpt: 16. Utrum anniversarium Dedicationis ecclesiae et sollemnitas patroni aut tituli ecclesiae in dominicam transferri possint? Resp.: Affirmative, si agitur de dominica per annum vel temporis Nativitatis et de anniversario Dedicationis ecclesiae propriae vel de patrono principali loci aut de titulo ecclesiae propriae, quae celebrantur tanquam sollemnitates.
